findings.summary: The pinned upstream webgpu 0.3.0 provider crashed before completing the WebGPU suite in all three clean processes, with SIGABRT or SIGSEGV worker signals around getWgslLanguageFeatures; an isolated provider probe also ended with SIGSEGV.

Doe completed the unchanged 13-assertion test process without a crash, but each clean process emitted 16 WGSL-to-SPIR-V translation failures and 16 createShaderModule failures, beginning with vector-plus-scalar compound assignment in hash22.

Doe's getCompilationInfo path returned no error-severity messages for native shader compilation failures, causing all 13 unchanged upstream assertions to report passed until the reviewed parent oracle rejected the native diagnostics.
The incumbent crashes and Doe fails the strengthened compilation oracle, so this run cannot establish provider equivalence, a reliability winner, or a public adoption claim.
The physical render node was inaccessible, neither provider passed the reviewed oracle, and this is a compilation-only workload, so the observed process durations cannot support a speed claim.

limitations: The pinned incumbent provider crashes before its adapter identity can be captured or any WebGPU compilation assertion can complete.
The workload compiles generated shaders but does not dispatch them, read back values, or test semantic output equivalence.
The unchanged upstream test does not emit each dynamically generated shader hash, so the receipt records source-owner and generated bundle hashes instead.
The host denied access to /dev/dri/renderD128, so the result is not physical-hardware evidence.

performance.reason: Neither provider passed the reviewed oracle, the workload is compilation-only, and the physical render node was inaccessible.

receiptOverhead.reason: The harness did not run matched traced and untraced samples, and neither provider produced a qualifying completion.

installation.summary: The Node loader is a controlled harness substitution, not a validated production installation path.

supportHardware.summary: The physical render node was inaccessible, and the incumbent crashed before adapter identity was available.

concurrency.summary: The diagnostic matrix used sequential clean processes rather than concurrent workload execution.

teardown.summary: Doe reached upstream cleanup, but the incumbent crashed and no promotion-scale teardown lane ran.

stress.summary: Three clean processes per provider establish diagnostic repeatability but do not satisfy the promotion stress policy.

memory.summary: Peak RSS was captured, but no bounded-growth leak test ran.

receipts.summary: The harness captured source hashes, provider failure boundaries, TAP identities, and native diagnostics, but lacks incumbent adapter identity, dynamic shader hashes, dispatch, readback, and output identity.

performance.summary: Neither provider passed the reviewed oracle and no physical GPU was accessible.

release.summary: The harness is not promoted and has no qualifying provider baseline.
